You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Inland Real Estate Corporation, realized ~2015-2017 record (outcome window fixed ~3-5 years after 2012)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The outcome window is fixed on Inland Real Estate
> Corporation's own realized record. This sub-dossier contains no information about how
> any transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status within the window (feasibility-relevant)
- The registrant's last public annual report is the Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015, filed February 26, 2016; it is the in-window annual report used as the primary outcome source. [SRC: SEC accession 0000923284-16-000069, Form 10-K (FY2015) cover]
- The company was acquired and taken private during the window, after which no further public audited annual reports were filed; the post-2016 portion of the window therefore has no public 10-K record and is not publicly observable (see final section). [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-110722, Form 15-12G]

## Realized record while still public (FY2015 10-K)
- Net income attributable to Inland Real Estate Corporation for the year ended December 31, 2015 was $25,531 (thousands). [SRC: SEC accession 0000923284-16-000069, Form 10-K (FY2015)]
- Net income attributable to common stockholders for FY2015 was $9,643 (thousands), a decrease of $19,166 compared with FY2014 ($28,809 thousands); FY2013 was $102,735 (thousands). [SRC: SEC accession 0000923284-16-000069, Form 10-K (FY2015)]
- The Company recorded approximately $222 (thousands) of impairment charges related to certain consolidated properties and investments in certain unconsolidated joint ventures for the year ended December 31, 2015. [SRC: SEC accession 0000923284-16-000069, Form 10-K (FY2015)]
- As of December 31, 2015 it owned interests in 133 investment properties including those owned through unconsolidated joint ventures, and fee simple interests in 96 investment properties excluding those joint ventures (down from 146 and 108, respectively, at year-end 2011). [SRC: SEC accession 0000923284-16-000069, Form 10-K (FY2015)]

## Documented status of the earlier-consolidated property (interface continuity over time)
- Orchard Crossing (Ft. Wayne, Indiana; approximately 130,129 gross leasable square feet) remained in the Company's consolidated portfolio as of December 31, 2015 at approximately 99% occupancy; it was retained, not divested, over the interval. [SRC: SEC accession 0000923284-16-000069, Form 10-K (FY2015) property tables]

## Transaction that terminated the public record
- On December 14, 2015 the Company entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with DRA Growth and Income Fund VIII, LLC ("Parent"), an affiliate of DRA Advisors LLC, and a merger subsidiary; under the agreement each outstanding common share would convert into the right to receive $10.60 in cash at the effective time. [SRC: SEC accession 0000923284-16-000069, Form 10-K (FY2015)]
- DRA Advisors LLC completed the acquisition effective March 30, 2016; Inland Real Estate Corporation survived as a wholly owned subsidiary and was renamed IRC Retail Centers, and common stock was converted into the $10.60-per-share cash consideration. [SRC: SEC accession 0000923284-16-000088, Form 8-K (filed 2016-03-30)]
- In connection with the closing, the common and preferred stock were delisted from the New York Stock Exchange via Form 25 and the company deregistered under the Exchange Act. [SRC: SEC accession 0000876661-16-000890, Form 25-NSE] [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-110722, Form 15-12G]

## No-record note (post-go-private segment of the window)
- Because the company was taken private and deregistered in 2016, there is no public audited annual report for the remainder of the ~2015-2017 window (i.e., FY2016 and FY2017 as an independent public reporting entity); that segment of the realized record is not publicly observable and is coded uncertain, with no figure inferred. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-110722, Form 15-12G]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Within the in-window public record, the whole company was acquired and taken private by DRA Advisors (effective March 30, 2016) for $10.60 per share in cash; through its last public annual report (FY2015) the business remained a going concern reporting positive net income ($25,531 thousands attributable to the Company; $9,643 thousands to common, down $19,166 year over year), a modestly reduced property count (133 interests vs. 146 at year-end 2011), only minor impairment ($222 thousands), and continued retention at ~99% occupancy of the retail center it had consolidated in 2011; the post-2016 private-ownership portion of the window has no public audited record and is coded uncertain. [SRC: SEC accession 0000923284-16-000069, Form 10-K (FY2015)] [SRC: SEC accession 0000923284-16-000088, Form 8-K (filed 2016-03-30)] [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-110722, Form 15-12G]

[SLICE END]
